questions.question: Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error. Has Gita any previous knowledge of work with junior colleagues?
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of the following sentence have been underlined and given as options. Select the option that contains an error.

Has Gita any previous knowledge of work with junior colleagues?
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is option 4) i.e. 'work.'

 

Key Points 

  • The error lies in the part 'work.'
  • We can note that the preposition 'of' is used before the word 'work,' which is a verb.
  • The word that must come after 'of' should be the object of the preposition 'of'. Hence, a gerund (working) must be placed after it.
  • A gerund is a verb that ends in '-ing' and functions as a noun or object.
  • Therefore we need to use the gerund form of the verb 'work'  which is 'working' after the preposition 'of.'
  • Therefore in the given sentence, we need to use 'working' in place of 'work' to make the sentence grammatically correct.
  • Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

 

Correct sentence: Has Gita any previous knowledge of working with junior colleagues?

questions.question: The following sentence has been split Into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. The sky appears blue as / it absorbs all colours / and reflects only blue / No error.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split Into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

The sky appears blue as / it absorbs all colours / and reflects only blue / No error.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "No error"

Key Points

  • "The sky appears blue as" – This clause essentially states that the sky looks blue because of a reason that's about to follow.
  • Grammatically, it's correct and can stand as an independent sentence.
  • "it absorbs all colours" – This part of the sentence is also grammatically correct as a dependent clause that explains why the sky looks blue.
  • It correctly uses the pronoun "it" to refer to the sky and the verb "absorbs" to describe what the sky does with all colours.
  • "and reflects only blue" – This is the final dependent clause connected to the sentence by the conjunction "and".
  • Its structure is parallel to the previous clause, and it further describes the behaviour of the sky concerning colours.

Therefore, the correct answer is "option 4".

Explanation:

  •  The error lies in option 1, which uses the incorrect preposition 'In'.
  •  The correct preposition to be used here should be 'of'.

  •  Using 'Of' forms the phrase 'Gets the better of'.
  •  Get the better of (someone)- gain an advantage over or defeat (someone) by superior strength or ability.

​
Thus, the rectified sentence is: She always gets the better of quarrels whether it is with girls or boys.

Confusion Points

  • "Get the better of (someone)" is a phrase. That's why 'the best' is not used here.
  • We often make silly mistakes in this type of question.

questions.question: Directions: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. At the last meeting / which took place in November, / half the members submitted / their resignations on protest.
questions.questionHtml:
Directions: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them contains an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options.

At the last meeting / which took place in November, / half the members submitted / their resignations on protest.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'their resignations on protest' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

Key Points

  • In the given sentence, the use of the preposition 'on' is incorrect.
  • The preposition 'on' means about something.
  • The use of the word 'protest' in the sentence indicates an action that shows that you do not like or approve of something.
  • Therefore, the preposition 'in' should be used in place of the preposition 'on'.
  • The preposition 'in' is used for showing the activity somebody is involved in.
     

Hence, the correct answer is option 2.

Correct Sentence: At the last meeting which took place in November, half the members submitted their resignations in protest.

Hinglish

  • दिए गए वाक्य में preposition 'on' का प्रयोग गलत है।
  • Preposition 'on' का अर्थ है किसी वस्‍तु के विषय में, किसी वस्‍तु पर।
  • वाक्य में 'protest' शब्द का प्रयोग किसी बात की नापसंदगी या अस्‍वीकृति दिखाने वाला वक्तव्‍य या कार्य; विरोध करने का संकेत देता है।
  • इसलिए, preposition 'in' का प्रयोग preposition 'on' के स्थान पर किया जाना चाहिए।
  • ऐसी गतिविधि दिखाने के लिए जिसमें कोई शामिल है हम preposition 'in' का उपयोग किया जाता है।
     

अतः सही उत्तर option 2 है।

सही वाक्य: At the last meeting which took place in November, half the members submitted their resignations in protest.

questions.question: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. He wondered what was the reason for her refusal to accompany him
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

He wondered what was the reason for her refusal to accompany him
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'was the reason'. 

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically incorrect. 
  • The erroneous Part 'was the reason' should be 'the reason was'. 
  • The given sentence is an example of direct to indirect transformation.
  • We know that when we change "a direct interrogative speech" into "indirect speech" the sentence is changed into "an assertive sentence". 
  • In these kinds of cases after the conjunction 'what' the subject 'the reason' should be used.
  • And then the verb 'was' should be used. 
  • Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2. 
    ​

Correct Sentence: He wondered what the reason was for her refusal to accompany him.

Guard over / making mistakes / by carefully checking / the assigned task.
questions.solution:
```html

The correct answer is 'Option 1' i.e. this part of the sentence has an error.

Key Points

  • The phrase "Guard over" is not idiomatic in this context.
  • The correct idiomatic expression should be "Guard against" when referring to preventing mistakes.
  • The rest of the sentence segments are grammatically correct and logically consistent.
  • Therefore, the segment "Guard over" should be corrected to "Guard against" to make the sentence grammatically correct.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Correct sentence: Guard against making mistakes by carefully checking the assigned task.

Additional Information

  • Option 2: "by carefully checking" - This phrase is grammatically correct and appropriately placed.
  • Option 3: "the assigned task" - This phrase correctly identifies the object of the sentence and is grammatically correct.
  • Option 4: "making mistakes" - This phrase correctly identifies the action to be guarded against and is grammatically correct.
```

questions.question: In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. questions.questionHtml:
In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.

As children tend to be highly impressionistic (1)/ one must be very careful for doing (2)/ or saying anything in their presence. (3)/ No Error (4)
questions.solution:
Correct option - 2

Here, concept of preposition is brought under consideration. Since, there are some words which take fixed preposition with them like accustomed with, careful of, obliged to, etc. Hence, replace for with of. Thus, option 2 is the correct answer.

Correct sentence - As children tend to be highly impressionistic one must be very careful of doing or saying anything in their presence.

questions.question: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If you had exercise regularly, you would have been fit today.
questions.questionHtml:
Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error.

If you had exercise regularly, you would have been fit today.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is 'exercise regularly'

Key Points

  • The aforementioned sentence is in past tense and we can notice the word 'had' before the error.
  • This implies that we need to use past participle in the sentence.
  • We can change the form of the verb into a past participle by adding -ed to the verb.
  • The correct verb form is exercised regularly

Hence, the correct sentence is: If you had exercised regularly, you would have been fit today.

Hint

  • Notice if there are auxiliary verbs such as has, have, or had before the erroneous part.
  • Generally, the past participle will be used with auxiliary verbs.

Additional Information

  • A verb can be changed into past tense by adding d,ed, or t.
  • Example:
    • work to worked(ed)
    • dance to danced(d)
    • deal to dealt(t)

questions.question: Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'. The smallest dog barks the loud.
questions.questionHtml:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose 'No error'.

The smallest dog barks the loud.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.
 
Key Points
  • The primary issue in the sentence is the use of "the loud" instead of the correct comparative form "the loudest".
  • In English, superlative forms are used to describe the highest degree of a quality among three or more items.
  • The correct phrase should be "the loudest", ensuring grammatical correctness and clarity.
  • Thus, the error is located in part 1 of the sentence.
Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.
 
Correct Sentence: "The smallest dog barks the loudest."
 
Additional Information
  • 2: "The smallest" – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
  • 3: "dog barks" – This part of the sentence is grammatically correct and does not require any changes.
  • 4: "No error" – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part 1.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. She was amazed by / the unique architecture of / the Sydney Opera House.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer.
She was amazed by / the unique architecture of / the Sydney Opera House.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is '1' i.e. No error .

Key Points

  • The given sentence is grammatically correct and there are no errors in any of the parts.
  • It is a simple declarative sentence that correctly uses the past tense ("was amazed") and the definite article ("the") before a proper noun ("Sydney Opera House").
  • The structure of the sentence follows standard English syntax and conveys the intended meaning clearly.

Correct sentence: She was amazed by the unique architecture of the Sydney Opera House.

Additional Information

  • The definite article "the" is used before a noun when the noun is specific and both the speaker and listener know what is being referred to.
  • "Unique" is correctly used as an adjective describing the noun "architecture."

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. It is commonly believed / that Democracy is / the best form / of the government.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

It is commonly believed / that Democracy is / the best form / of the government.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is: of the government.

Key Points

  • The phrase "of the government" should be "of government" to be grammatically correct.
  • The article "the" is unnecessary here and makes the phrase awkward.
  • In standard English usage, "government" does not need a definite article in this context.
  • Correct usage would be "the best form of government" without the article "the" before "government".

Correct sentence: It is commonly believed that Democracy is the best form of government.
